Note: Expected 7 OnNewRecord firings, got 1. The runner raises a part page's OnNewRecord ONCE for opening a card over an EMPTY part; this arm asserts 6 (or 7 with New()), the figure measured on bc-linux across all 8 cloud legs of corpus run 34140530877. That number is NOT settled: the official Microsoft Windows container answers 3 (and 4 with New()) for the same arms — nightly run 34182689878 — and the bc-linux figure is under investigation as a possible defect in that tier rather than a rendering difference. So this entry records a measured disagreement about the empty-part OPENING COST, and deliberately does not assert which tier is right. It is a known gap and not an expect-divergence for exactly that reason: divergence would claim the runner's answer is intended and permanent, which is not a claim anything currently supports. The DELTAS the same file asserts — landing on an existing data row 0, stepping onto the draft line +1, writing into a started draft line +0, a second row +1 — are agreed by both tiers, and the runner now matches all of them; DraftLine_ReachedByNextThenWritten_RunsOnNewRecordExactlyOnce is the arm that measures only those, and it PASSES, which is why it no longer has an entry here. Tracked as #3029 (the firing count) and #3481 (which absolute number is correct). Upstream corpus PR #284 re-scopes these arms to assert the deltas instead of the tier-specific constant; when that merges and the pin advances, these entries should go.
